result.headline: A practical primer on how large language models are trained and deployed
key_takeaways: Large language models are trained in two broad phases: pretraining on large text corpora, then fine-tuning for instruction-following.
Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is commonly used to align model outputs with human preferences.
Model performance scales predictably with data, parameters, and compute, following well-studied scaling laws.
Deploying these models safely requires guardrails such as content filtering, rate limiting, and human oversight.
Smaller, distilled models can approximate larger ones for latency- and cost-sensitive applications.
